name: Burnley

licensing.selective: Selective licensing in parts of Burnley Wood with Healey Wood and the Leyland Road area (July 2022 to July 2027), and in parts of Trinity, Daneshouse, Gannow, Queensgate and Padiham (a later designation following a 2024 consultation). A consultation on changes to the schemes closed on 18 October 2026; the existing schemes continue meanwhile.
licensing.fee: £736 (Burnley Wood and Leyland Road) or £774 (Trinity, Daneshouse, Gannow, Queensgate and Padiham) for an online selective licence application, with discounts for accredited landlords

housing: Burnley's housing is dominated by Victorian terraced houses built for the cotton mills, many of them two-up two-down, and house prices are among the lowest in England. A large share of these terraces are privately rented, and some streets have high numbers of empty homes. The outer areas such as Briercliffe and Worsthorne have semis, newer houses and stone cottages. Check with the council whether any licensing scheme applies to a property before letting it.
checkinTips: Victorian stone and brick terraces: photograph back yards, outside toilets or stores, gutters and any damp on party walls.
Two-up two-down houses: photograph the boiler, meters (often in the cellar or under the stairs) and the cellar for damp.
Cellar dwellings and basements: photograph walls and floors for damp and record any dehumidifier or pump.
Stone cottages in Worsthorne and the moorland villages: photograph windows, roofs and walls for wind-driven rain damage.
Converted mill buildings and flats above shops in the town centre: photograph the communal entrance, stairs and meter cupboards, and count every key and fob.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe homes to Burnley Borough Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect and take action against landlords.
